analyst_notes: Eval-0 (epic-story): Non-discriminating on correctness — baseline read source code and produced correct commands. Discriminates only on efficiency (2x tokens, 2.5x time).

Eval-1 (task-lifecycle): Key discriminating eval. Baseline read source code but still got the `tools` namespace wrong for task commands (used `oraculo task *` instead of `oraculo tools task *`). This is the most important correctness signal.
Eval-2 (approval-knowledge): Non-discriminating on correctness — baseline read source code and got it right. Discriminates on efficiency only.
The `correct-command-namespace` assertion in eval-0 is non-discriminating when the agent has access to the source code. Consider adding it to eval-1 explicitly.
The skill provides both correctness AND efficiency gains. In production installs (no source code), the gap would be much larger — the skill is the only reference available.
